newsitem.title: USA: Clinton denies soliciting money at White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton denies soliciting money at White House.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday denied there was any solicitation of money or "a price tag" on the coffee meetings he held with potential supporters at the White House.

Asked at a news conference whether the coffees broke or at least skirted laws prohibiting the raising of campaign funds on federal property, Clinton said: "No. We got strict advice about what the rules were ... There was no solicitation at the events ... and the guidelines made clear there was to be no price tag on the events."

Clinton fielded questions on the growing campaign finance controversy during a joint news conference with Chilean President Eduardo Frei. It came one day after the White House released internal memos showing Clinton had encouraged inviting major Democratic party campaign donors to White House events to energize further support.
As he had on Tuesday, the president defended that policy as one merely showing gratitude to friends and supporters and aimed at drumming up future backing.

"I don't think people who support you and help you through tough times, who believe in what you're doing, should be disqualified from being the president's guests at the White House," he said. "The costs were not borne by the taxpayers."

He declined to comment on rising pressures for appointment of a special prosecutor on the fund-raising issue, saying it was up to the attorney general to request that on the merits and adding, "It should not be a political decision." But he said he thought nothing in the documents released on Tuesday would require a special prosecutor's appointment.
